summary: A dense engine-building game where you design a zoo, playing cards to build enclosures, acquire animals, and trigger conservation projects while juggling appeal, reputation, and a tight action-economy where card slots determine how powerful each action is. It plays slow and cerebral, rewarding a long-view engine that only starts paying off in the back half of the game.
praised: deep, satisfying engine-building with a strong theme
gorgeous animal art and production value
high replayability from varied player powers and card pool
criticised: long playtime and heavy analysis paralysis, especially with new players
steep learning curve and rulebook complexity
slow start can feel unrewarding until the engine kicks in
conservation/appeal icon soup takes a while to parse

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light drafting competition
interaction.detail: Each player builds their own zoo on a private board and mostly optimizes their own engine, but there is competition over which animal and sponsor cards are available to draft and over shared conservation project thresholds. Turn order and icon count on the shared action cards create some indirect jostling, but boards otherwise develop independently.

scoring.why: Final score blends appeal-based points, conservation project points, and end-game bonus cards, so no single scoring source dominates.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by building an efficient engine of animals, enclosures, and sponsors that generates appeal and conservation points faster than your opponents across the mid-to-late game.
